summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen, retired champion pugilist of the world, died at the Baptist hospital on April 5, 1903, and recounted a career that ended with a win over Jim Stewart in England in 1879.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Globe-Democrat, Monday Morning, April 6, 1903, page 1.

facts.fact: Allen died at the Baptist hospital, Garrison and Franklin avenues, St. Louis, at 7:35 a.m. after being very low for several days
places: Baptist hospital, Garrison and Franklin avenues, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen had been taken to the Baptist hospital a week before the Friday preceding his death
Allen was born at Birmingham, England, April 23, 1839
By his own official record Allen fought fourteen prize ring matches in England and ten in America
Allen's last fight was against Jim Stewart in England, for £50 a side; it lasted fifty-five minutes and sixteen rounds and was won by Allen
At his death Allen's saloon was 'Tom Allen's Champion's Rest,' 619 Market Street, where he had served drinks and told sporting stories
places: Champion's Rest, 619 Market Street, St. Louis
